# Offer Letter Package: John Stiles (REQ-2291)

## 1. Offer Letter

**Brightwater Analytics, Inc.**
Austin, Texas

November 10, 2025

John Stiles
[Street address]
San Diego, California [ZIP]

Dear John,

We are pleased to offer you employment with Brightwater Analytics, Inc. (the "Company") on the terms below.

**1. Position**
You will be employed as a **[Software Engineer II (L4)]**. This is a full-time, exempt position. You will report to Mary Major, Engineering Manager, and work remotely from California.

**2. Compensation**
Your annual base salary will be **[$175,000]**. It is subject to applicable withholdings and paid on the Company's regular payroll schedule.

**3. Equity**
You will be granted **[3,200]** restricted stock units (RSUs). The RSUs vest over four years with a one-year cliff, subject to your continued service. The grant is governed by the Company's equity incentive plan and your RSU award agreement. If those documents conflict with this letter, they control.

**4. Signing Bonus**
You will receive a one-time signing bonus of **$20,000** (gross), payable in your first regular paycheck.

If you resign voluntarily before completing 12 months of employment, you agree to repay a pro-rated portion of the bonus, calculated as follows:

> $20,000 × (12 − full months worked) ÷ 12

The Company will not deduct any repayment amount from your final wages unless you give separate written authorization at that time.

**5. Start Date**
Your anticipated start date is **Monday, December 1, 2025**.

**6. Benefits**
You will be eligible for the Company's benefits programs, subject to their terms, as described in the enclosed Benefits Guide.

**7. Contingencies**
This offer is contingent on:
- satisfactory completion of a background check, conducted in accordance with applicable law; and
- proof of your identity and authorization to work in the United States, as required by federal law, within three business days of your start date.

**8. At-Will Employment**
Your employment is at will. Either you or the Company may end it at any time, with or without cause or notice. Only a written agreement signed by the Company's CEO can change the at-will nature of your employment.

**9. Governing Law**
This letter is governed by California law. Any dispute arising from your employment will be resolved in the state or federal courts located in California. Nothing in this letter requires you to adjudicate a claim outside California or deprives you of the substantive protection of California law.

**10. Acceptance**
This letter, together with the documents it references, is the complete statement of your offer. It supersedes any prior discussions or representations, whether oral or written.

To accept, please sign and return this letter by **[November 14, 2025]**.

We are excited to have you join the team.

Sincerely,

______________________
[Name], [Title]
Brightwater Analytics, Inc.

**Accepted:**

______________________ Date: __________
John Stiles

---

## 2. Cover Note to Mary Major

**To:** Mary Major
**Re:** John Stiles offer: hold before sending

Mary, the draft letter uses only approved terms. The verbal offer from Nov 7 does not match REQ-2291 in several places. Please confirm the items below before we send anything.

| # | Item | Promised | Approved / required | Recommendation | Sign-off |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Title / level | Senior Software Engineer | Software Engineer II (L4) | Send at L4. If you believe he is L5, re-level the requisition first. | VP Engineering + Finance (amended req) |
| 2 | Base salary | $182,000 | Band maximum $175,000 | Offer $175,000. Otherwise get a band exception, or a re-level that fits $182k. | VP Engineering + Finance |
| 3 | RSUs | 4,000 | 3,200 (Comp Committee, Oct 28) | Offer 3,200. The extra 800 would need new approval. | Compensation Committee |
| 4 | Non-compete | "Standard" | Void for California employees (B&P §16600) | Removed from the letter. The recruiter's statement was incorrect and should be corrected with John. | Legal (confirm) |
| 5 | Governing law / venue | Texas, Travis County (template) | Labor Code §925 | Changed to California law and California courts. | Legal (confirm) |
| 6 | Bonus repayment | Full repayment (template) | Pro-rated for California hires; no wage deduction | Updated in the letter. The $20k amount is within approval. | None |

The $20,000 signing bonus and the Dec 1 start date already match the approval.

**Bracketed items:**
- Title, base salary and RSUs show the approved values. Change them only if the sign-offs above are obtained in writing.
- The acceptance deadline is a proposed date. Please confirm it.

**Next steps:**
1. The recruiter should call John today to reset expectations on the gaps (items 1–4) before the letter goes out.
2. Please send me your decision on items 1–3 by [date].

---

## 3. Worked Example: Signing-Bonus Repayment

**Scenario:** John resigns voluntarily after 7 full months of employment.

| Step | Calculation | Result |
|---|---|---|
| Bonus paid | | $20,000.00 |
| Monthly earned portion | $20,000 ÷ 12 | $1,666.67 |
| Full months worked | | 7 |
| Unearned months | 12 − 7 | 5 |
| **Amount owed** | $20,000 × 5 ÷ 12 | **$8,333.33** |

John would repay **$8,333.33**. The other $11,666.67 is his to keep.

The Company may not deduct this amount from his final paycheck unless he provides separate written authorization at that time. Without that authorization, the Company would invoice him for repayment.

Payroll should confirm whether repayment is calculated on the gross or net amount, so the tax treatment is handled correctly.
